basis: Disorder of synovial tissue, a component of joints and the locomotor system.
Defined as isolated breast/nipple aplasia, outside the axes; meatal stenosis in one reported male is insufficient to establish typical urinary involvement.
Retinal synaptic dysfunction defines disease; developmental impairment in 4/6 and hyperglycemia reflecting endocrine dysfunction in 3/4 support additional axes.
Intellectual disability defines disease; strabismus and frontal balding each occur in 30-79%. Facial shape and short stature alone do not establish locomotor damage.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability, spasticity and ataxia define neurologic disease; hyperopia reported in 1/1. DNA repair deficiency alone is not metabolic disease; immunodeficiency absent.
Malignant endothelial tumor arising in lymphatic vessels, mapped to the vascular axis; this is not lymphoma. Additional organs depend on the tumor site.
Immune-mediated destruction of cerebellar neurons; associated malignancies are separate diseases, and ocular symptoms do not establish eye damage.
Symptomatic Coffin-Lowry phenotype includes variable neurodevelopmental impairment and characteristic skeletal abnormalities; dental and cardiovascular abnormalities are only occasional.
Benign tumor arising in the nail matrix; nails belong to the dermatologic axis.
Urothelial carcinoma arising from urachal epithelium of the urinary bladder.
Placental obstetric disorder lies outside the axes; hemorrhage alone does not establish a primary blood or coagulation disease.
Sarcoma originates in the larynx, which belongs to the pulmonary axis; soft-tissue histology does not establish locomotor involvement.
Mucosal outpouchings within the gallbladder wall; gallbladder and biliary tract belong to the hepatic axis.
Immune-associated painful cutaneous ecchymoses with dermal inflammation; coagulation abnormalities are occasional and do not establish a primary blood disorder.
Inborn pentose metabolism defect causing benign L-xylulose excretion; urinary carbohydrate does not indicate kidney damage.
Chronic immune-mediated airway inflammation, obstruction and remodeling define asthma; triggers and associated conditions do not establish other organ damage.
Brain malformations, epilepsy and severe developmental impairment define disease; strabismus occurs in 3/5. Dysphagia and hypotonia reflect neurologic dysfunction, not separate organ damage.
Inflammatory vasculitis specifically affecting brain or spinal cord vessels defines vascular, neurologic and immune involvement.
Inherited degeneration or dysfunction of retinal cone photoreceptors causes impaired central and color vision.
Focal tibial peripheral nerve dysfunction; resulting weakness does not establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Thyroid hormone deficiency from birth; lasting neurologic injury chiefly follows prolonged untreated deficiency and is not established in most patients across this umbrella.
Defined by hydrocephalus and posterior fossa malformations plus a cutaneous capillary malformation; eyelid nevus does not itself establish ocular dysfunction.
Endocrine overactivity, characteristic pigmentation/cutaneous myxomas and cardiac myxomas are major diagnostic features; schwannomas and skeletal lesions are occasional.
Aortic disease and skeletal connective-tissue abnormalities define disease; permanent dermal striae occur in 24/70 (34%). Dural ectasia without demonstrated functional damage is excluded.
Congenital eyelid and canthal malformation; systemic syndromes sometimes associated with it are separate diagnoses.
